name: 叶屋（手打ちうどん叶屋） (Kanoya (Handmade Udon))

claims.text: No gluten-free noodle alternative or dedicated gluten-free prep process was found in any source; the shop's entire menu centers on hand-made wheat udon.
The house dashi is made with katsuobushi (bonito flakes) and iriko (dried sardines) alongside kombu, and is used as the base for the broth across the menu; no plant-based dashi option was found.

The broth is made from scratch with Rishiri kelp, bonito, and dried sardines, with no added chemical seasoning (no MSG) — a plus for diners avoiding additives, though it is not a GF/vegan accommodation.
The menu has both English and Japanese, and the staff can speak English, so ordering and asking about ingredients is not a problem.
The restaurant is certified halal and also lists vegetarian dishes such as salads and dips alongside its kebab-focused menu.
The restaurant's own listing notes that guests with extensive allergies or strong food dislikes may have their reservation declined, since the menu is a single fixed omakase course.
The chefs make their coconut milk and curry pastes (nam prik gaeng) from scratch in-house rather than using pre-made bases, giving them more direct control over ingredients than many Thai kitchens.

Mitarashi-style dango sauce is conventionally made with soy sauce (shoyu), sugar, and starch; soy sauce produced in Japan is usually wheat-brewed, so mitarashi dango is generally not considered gluten-free unless a shop confirms otherwise — this is a general caution about the dish style, not a statement specific to Kikuya.

The shop's two named specialty items are built from plant-based staples — daifuku is mochi rice and Tokachi azuki beans with sugar, and the dango base is jōshinko (rice flour) — with the official site emphasizing no additives and domestic ingredient sourcing, though this describes ingredient philosophy rather than a formal allergen or vegan certification.

name: 駒形どぜう 本店 (Komagata Dozeu (Honten))

claims.text: The house dojō-nabe broth is a shōyu-based warishita typical of this dish style; conventional Japanese soy sauce is wheat-brewed, so the broth is not inherently gluten-free. This is general knowledge about the dish type, not a restaurant-specific confirmed statement.
The menu is built entirely around dojō (pond loach) and other fish-based items prepared in a shared kitchen; no vegetarian or vegan dish was identified in any menu listing found online.
Skewers are coated in panko (wheat breadcrumbs) before deep-frying.
Dipping is done in a shared Osaka-style Worcestershire-type sauce, with a house 'no double-dipping' rule since the sauce pot is communal.

The confirmed menu is fish-, meat-, and dairy-based (pork fillet katsu, ham katsu, cheese, quail egg, squid, shrimp, chikuwa fish cake, shiso-wrapped pork belly); no vegetable-only or plant-based skewers were found in any source reviewed.

name: 松太郎 新宿小滝橋通り店 (Matsutaro Shinjuku Kotakibashi-dori)

claims.text: The shop's signature dish is shoyu ramen made with a tare blended from four different soy sauces — standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.

The shio (salt) ramen broth is seasoned with salt and kombu extract but also includes a hidden seafood dashi as a secret ingredient, and the shoyu ramen uses a soy-based tare — no vegan or plant-only broth option was identified.
なぎ食堂 (vegan shokudo) in Shibuya Uguisudani-cho closed on December 23, 2023 after operating 16 years since 2007; owner pivoted to catering and event food services.
Tabelog now lists the Shibuya location with the 【移転】(relocated/closed) tag rather than as an operating restaurant.
Celiac review: the restaurant had limited gluten-free options — no soup or warm food was gluten free on the entire menu; the green salad was the solitary safe option.
Search corroboration that the Uguisudani-cho storefront (Shibuya-ku Uguisudanicho 15-10) permanently closed 2023-12-23 and did not relocate to a replacement Shibuya storefront.

The kitchen prepares no meat, fish, or animal products at all — every dish on the menu is vegan by default, so there is no risk of animal-product cross-contact from shared equipment with non-vegan dishes.
The restaurant uses no meat, fish, eggs, or dairy in any dish, making it explicitly safe for customers with egg and dairy allergies as well as vegans/vegetarians.
